answer.evidence: The base (rows 24-31) is the main volume. Its width profile goes 8, 10, 12 and back to 10, 8, so it reads as a rounded ellipse. Rows 25-27 are the visible top with the shaft entering it. Row 28 (#f4b370) is a lighter front-edge line, and a darker row 29 follows. Rows 29-31 are the darker front face. The thin shaft (rows 18-23, width 2), the crossbar and ring arms (rows 13-17) and the sun and planets are slender details on top of this base.

styleAnswer.evidence: The orrery is a small, thin prop: a gold stand with a few small spheres and rings. The per-tile median of 0 only reflects its size, so I judged density by eye. On the measured facts it matches the thin references: 16 distinct colours against 14 for the bench and the lamp. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines carry a tint (dark brown/gold) rather than a black sticker line. The gold stand and the spheres show about 4 lightness steps with highlight dots, close to the bench and lamp, though a little less than the richer stall and well. It does not look flatter or more sticker-like than the bench or the lamp, so I accept it next to them.

answer.evidence: The main body is a round base at rows 24-31 with a 2-row outline and rim at the top (dark outline at row 24, lighter rim at row 25). Below it is a front face of about 6 rows shaded for a rounded bottom (widths 12, then 10, then 8). The base has no ellipse opening, no contents, and no front-edge line followed by eave shadow. Above it is a 2px-wide shaft (rows 18-23) with a crossbar and small spheres at rows 11-17. These are drawn face-on with no horizontal surfaces. The object reads as a front elevation with only a rim on top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The orrery is a small, thin prop: a tripod base, a central stem and arms ending in small spheres. The per-tile median of 0 means the piece is smaller than one tile, so the density fact does not count against it. It has 16 distinct colours, slightly above the thin references (bench 14, lamp 14), and flat-fill coverage is 0%. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline carries a tint and reads as a dark version of the adjacent material. This avoids the near-black sticker look of the lamp, which is 100% neutral. The spheres and arms show highlight, mid and dark steps, about 4 in total against 5 on the references. It is a little simpler than the bench and lamp but would sit next to them without looking flatter or more sticker-like. It is not as rich as the stall or well, which are much larger objects.

Its 16 distinct colours are above the bench (14) and the crook lamp (14), the two references of similar thinness.
